title: Create a new area scheme by cloning an existing one
task: Create a new AreaScheme by copying an existing one with ElementTransformUtils.CopyElement, then renaming it uniquely. AreaScheme has no Create and no Duplicate, and IsGrossBuildingArea is read-only and inherited from the clone source.

pitfalls.symptom: There is no obvious way to make a new area scheme: AreaScheme has no Create method, and ElementType.Duplicate(name) is not available on it.
pitfalls.cause: AreaScheme derives from Element, not ElementType, so it has no Duplicate; there is no factory for it either.
pitfalls.fix: Clone an existing scheme with ElementTransformUtils.CopyElement(doc, sourceScheme.Id, XYZ.Zero) (translation is irrelevant, a scheme has no geometry). The returned collection holds the new element id(s); the new AreaScheme is the one whose GetElement casts to AreaScheme.

pitfalls.symptom: You cannot set whether the new scheme is a Gross Building scheme; AreaScheme.IsGrossBuildingArea has no setter.
pitfalls.cause: IsGrossBuildingArea is read-only and is inherited from whatever scheme you copied.
pitfalls.fix: Choose the clone source by the kind you want: copy the scheme whose IsGrossBuildingArea is true for a gross plan, or a Rentable/BOMA scheme for a net plan. You cannot flip it afterwards.

pitfalls.symptom: Setting the clone's Name throws that the name is already in use.
pitfalls.cause: Area scheme names must be unique; the copy is auto-named '<source> 1', and blindly assigning a fixed name can collide.
pitfalls.fix: Gather existing AreaScheme.Name values first and pick an unused name (append a counter) before assigning created.Name.
